::: {.callout-tip}
### Goal of DM
**DM provides the subject-level backbone** for SDTM: **one record per subject** with core identifiers, demographics, key reference dates, and planned/actual treatment assignment — enabling **traceability**, **reviewability**, and **submission readiness**.
:::

## What DM is
**DM (Demographics)** is a **Special-Purpose** SDTM domain containing **one record per subject**.  
It anchors **subject identity** and **study timing**, and supports links to other domains using `USUBJID`.

## Why it matters (reviewer value)
Reviewers typically start with DM to confirm:
- **Who** is in the study (subject IDs + demographics)
- **When** participation occurred (reference dates)
- **What** arm/treatment context applies (planned vs actual)
- **Whether** counts reconcile across SDTM domains (AE/EX/DS/etc.)

## What you’ll find here
- **Purpose:** Subject-level SDTM “spine” (one record per subject)
- **Grain:** **1 record per `USUBJID`**
- **Traceability:** Source/EDC → DM → downstream SDTM domains → ADaM → TLFs
- **Review value:** Clean joins, consistent subject counts, transparent arm + reference-date definitions

---

## Core identifiers (always expected)
DM typically includes:
- `STUDYID` — Study identifier  
- `DOMAIN` — Always `"DM"`  
- `USUBJID` — Unique subject identifier (join key across SDTM)  
- `SUBJID` — Subject ID as collected  
- `SITEID` — Site identifier (if applicable)

---

## Timing anchors (reference dates)
DM is where reviewers commonly look first for **study participation timing**. Typical anchors include:
- `RFSTDTC` — Subject reference start date/time (ISO 8601 character)
- `RFENDTC` — Subject reference end date/time (ISO 8601 character)
- `RFXSTDTC` / `RFXENDTC` — Exposure reference start/end (if used/available)
- `DTHDTC` — Death date/time (if applicable)

::: {.callout-note}
### SDTM date/time conventions (`--DTC`)
SDTM `--DTC` variables are **character ISO 8601**. Partial dates (and imputation conventions, if any) must be **consistent** and documented in **define.xml** (Origin/MethodDefs) and the **cSDRG** narrative.
:::

---

## Demographics variables (typical)
Common demographics include:
- `AGE`, `AGEU` (e.g., YEARS)
- `SEX`
- `RACE`
- `ETHNIC` (when collected/required)
- `COUNTRY` (when applicable)

---

## Treatment assignment (planned vs actual)
DM commonly carries both **planned** and **actual** assignment:
- `ARM`, `ARMCD` — Planned arm / coded arm
- `ACTARM`, `ACTARMCD` — Actual arm / coded actual arm

SDTMIG v3.4 also highlights variables that help explain **mismatches**:
- `ARMNRS` — Reason subject did not receive expected treatment
- `ACTARMUD` — Actual arm derivation details / explanation (useful when `ACTARM` is derived)

::: {.callout-note}
### Common submission convention (helps reviewer interpretation)
- **Screen failures** (if included): keep `ARM/ARMCD/ACTARM/ACTARMCD` **blank**
- **Randomized but not treated:** populate `ARM/ARMCD`, keep `ACTARM/ACTARMCD` **blank**
:::

---

## Mini example (one record per subject)

| STUDYID | DOMAIN | USUBJID | SUBJID | SITEID | AGE | AGEU | SEX | RACE  | ARM    | ACTARM | RFSTDTC     |
|---|---|---|---|---|---:|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| ABC123 | DM | ABC123-001-1001 | 1001 | 001 | 62 | YEARS | M | WHITE | Drug A | Drug A | 2025-01-15 |

---

## Traceability checklist (review-friendly)
To make DM “submission clean,” reviewers expect:
- **Clear origins** for each variable (define.xml Origin)
- **Explainable derivations** (MethodDefs where applicable)
- **Consistent arm logic** (ARM vs ACTARM; document exceptions)
- **Consistent `--DTC` creation rules** (including partial/missing handling)
- **Counts reconcile** to subject disposition / enrollment tracking

A typical traceability narrative:
**Source/EDC/CRF → DM → other SDTM domains → ADaM → TLFs**

---

## Common QC checks for DM
- Exactly **1 record per `USUBJID`** (no duplicates)
- `USUBJID` uniqueness and consistent formatting
- `RFSTDTC` present for enrolled/treated subjects as expected
- Planned vs actual arm rules applied consistently and explainably
- Demographics completeness (SEX/AGE/RACE) per protocol expectations
- Cross-domain consistency (e.g., subjects in AE/EX exist in DM)

---

## Version note (portfolio-friendly)
Aligned to **SDTMIG v3.4** and the SDTM conceptual model (**SDTM v2.0**, published **29-Nov-2021**).  
FDA announced support beginning for **SDTM v2.0 / SDTMIG v3.4** in a Federal Register notice (**Dec 13, 2023**).
